content:
Here is some information supplied by the email account provider:

When creating a new folder, the server shows error: "{imaps} Bad flag in APPEND command: Nonjunk"

The error is clear — the IMAP server is rejecting the APPEND command because Thunderbird is sending two junk-related flags simultaneously:

$notjunk — a valid IMAP keyword flag NonJunk — a non-standard flag (no backslash prefix) that the server doesn't accept

This is a Thunderbird-side behavior — it's sending both $notjunk and NonJunk together when moving messages to newly created folders, and the server's IMAP parser rejects NonJunk as invalid.

content:
The first thing to do is to verify that you're using the correct server settings. Here are my working Gmail settings for comparison (the SMTP settings are most relevant in this case):

Incoming Server Type: IMAP Mail Server Incoming Server Name: imap.gmail.com Port: 993 User Name: <my email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: OAuth2

SMTP Server Name: smtp.gmail.com Port: 465 Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: OAuth2 User Name: <my email address>

(if you're set up as a POP account, use these settings:)

Incoming Server Type: POP Mail Server Incoming Server Name: pop.gmail.com Port: 995 User Name: <my email address> Connection Security: SSL/TLS Authentication method: OAuth2


If these are correct, you may need to re-authenticate, which Google forces us all to do every once in a while. To do that,

- Make sure cookies are allowed (see <settings | privacy & security web content accept cookies from sites) - delete existing gmail (see <settings sites show cookies) any stored password entries <settings saved passwords>. < p></settings>

(the first step is the most important one - the others may not be necessary.)

Don't discount that Bitdefender isn't the problem. You should test it by creating an exception for Thunderbird, or, better yet, by temporarily disabling Bitdefender while you try to send a message. If you're using Windows, you can re-start in Safe Mode with Networking to do this.

content:
This just means that a spammer has gotten hold of your email address and is sending out spam impersonating you. Unfortunately, there is nothing you can do about it. It's not originating from you.

Often or usually the "From:" address shows your real name but a patently wrong address. Of course, many recipients just see your name and gloss over the address. Nothing you can do about that either, except to alert your contacts to be skeptical about such messages and to not respond to them or click any links in them. Once you learn to recognize the obvious signs they're pretty easy to recognize.

I get similar messages almost every day that purport to be from my family, usually saying something like, "I forgot to send you these pictures" and providing a link to a probably malware site. I just mark them as Spam and move on.
